pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMPLE POEMS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is a poem different from a passage?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the persona in a given poem
2. identify instances of repetition in a given poem
3. explain what the poem is about
4. appreciate the role of poems in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMPLE POEMS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: SIMPLE POEMS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the persona in a given poem

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the persona in a given poem. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the persona in a given poem.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the persona in a given poem. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify instances of repetition in a given poem

What this means
In this part you learn to identify instances of repetition in a given poem. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify instances of repetition in a given poem.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify instances of repetition in a given poem. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Explain what the poem is about

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what the poem is about. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what the poem is about.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what the poem is about. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the role of poems in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of poems in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of poems in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of poems in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the persona in a given poem)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems to a partner. (skill: identify instances of repetition in a given poem)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: explain what the poem is about)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate the role of poems in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the persona in a given poem.
3. Practise this skill: identify instances of repetition in a given poem.
4. Practise this skill: explain what the poem is about.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is a poem different from a passage?
2. How can you say what is in the poem in your own words?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the persona in a given poem.
5. Be able to: identify instances of repetition in a given poem.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
